claim: Storage Gateway supports four hybrid cloud use cases: move backups and archives to the cloud, reduce on-premises storage with cloud-backed file shares, give on-premises applications low-latency access to data stored in AWS, and give data lake access for pre and post processing workflows.
question: What use cases does AWS Storage Gateway support?

values.display: four key hybrid cloud use cases

qualifiers.scope: AWS Storage Gateway, all gateway types

evidence.quote: Storage Gateway supports four key hybrid cloud use cases – (1) move backups and archives to the cloud, (2) reduce on-premises storage with cloud-backed file shares, (3) provide on-premises applications low-latency access to data stored in AWS, and (4) data lake access for pre and post processing workflows.

claim: Storage Gateway lets you reduce your on-premises storage footprint and associated costs by using AWS storage services.
question: Why should I use AWS Storage Gateway?

values.display: reduce your on-premises storage footprint

evidence.quote: AWS Storage Gateway enables you to reduce your on-premises storage footprint and associated costs by leveraging AWS storage services.

claim: Storage Gateway gives on-premises applications three types of storage interfaces: file, volume, and tape.
question: What storage interfaces does Storage Gateway give to on-premises applications?

values.display: file, volume, and tape

evidence.quote: Depending on your use case, Storage Gateway provides three types of storage interfaces for your on-premises applications: file, volume, and tape.

claim: Amazon S3 File Gateway stores and retrieves objects in Amazon S3 through file protocols such as NFS and SMB, and objects written through it can be accessed directly in S3.
question: How does Amazon S3 File Gateway give on-premises applications access to S3?

values.display: Network File System (NFS) and Server Message Block (SMB)

evidence.quote: The Amazon S3 File Gateway enables you to store and retrieve objects in Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3) using file protocols such as Network File System (NFS) and Server Message Block (SMB). Objects written through S3 File Gateway can be directly accessed in S3.

claim: Volume Gateway gives on-premises applications block storage over iSCSI, stores the volume data in Amazon S3, and lets you take point-in-time copies of volumes as Amazon EBS snapshots.
question: What does Volume Gateway provide and where is the data stored?

values.display: block storage to your on-premises applications using iSCSI connectivity

evidence.quote: The Volume Gateway provides block storage to your on-premises applications using iSCSI connectivity. Data on the volumes is stored in Amazon S3 and you can take point-in-time copies of volumes that are stored in AWS as Amazon EBS snapshots.

claim: Tape Gateway gives a backup application an iSCSI virtual tape library interface; virtual tapes are stored in Amazon S3 and can be archived to S3 Glacier or S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
question: What does Tape Gateway provide to a backup application, and where do the tapes go?

values.display: iSCSI virtual tape library (VTL) interface

evidence.quote: The Tape Gateway provides your backup application with an iSCSI virtual tape library (VTL) interface, consisting of a virtual media changer, virtual tape drives, and virtual tapes. Virtual tapes are stored in Amazon S3 and can be archived to Amazon S3 Glacier or Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.

claim: On premises, you can deploy a Storage Gateway virtual machine on VMware ESXi, Microsoft Hyper-V, Linux KVM or Nutanix AVM, or deploy a hardware appliance; you can also deploy it in VMware Cloud on AWS or as an AMI in Amazon EC2.
question: Where can I deploy an AWS Storage Gateway appliance?

values.display: VMware ESXi, Microsoft Hyper-V, Linux KVM, Nutanix AVM

evidence.quote: On-premises, you can deploy a virtual machine containing the Storage Gateway software on VMware ESXi, Microsoft Hyper-V, Linux KVM, Nutanix AVM, or you can deploy Storage Gateway as a hardware appliance. You can also deploy the Storage Gateway VM in VMware Cloud on AWS, or as an AMI in Amazon EC2.

claim: In cached mode, Volume Gateway writes the primary data to S3 and keeps frequently accessed data in a local cache for low-latency access.
question: What is cached mode of Volume Gateway?

values.display: your primary data is written to S3

evidence.quote: In the cached mode, your primary data is written to S3, while retaining your frequently accessed data locally in a cache for low-latency access.

claim: In stored mode, Volume Gateway keeps the primary data locally, so the entire dataset is available for low-latency access, and backs it up to AWS asynchronously.
question: What is stored mode of Volume Gateway?

values.display: your primary data is stored locally

evidence.quote: In the stored mode, your primary data is stored locally and your entire dataset is available for low-latency access while asynchronously backed up to AWS.

claim: You can manage backup and retention policies for the cached and stored volume modes of Volume Gateway through AWS Backup.
question: What AWS Storage Gateway types can I manage through AWS Backup?

values.display: cached and stored volume modes of Volume Gateway

evidence.quote: You can manage backup and retention policies for cached and stored volume modes of Volume Gateway through AWS Backup.

claim: The maximum supported size of the local cache for a gateway running on a virtual machine is 64 TiB.
question: What is the maximum supported size of the local cache per gateway?

values.display: 64 TiB

qualifiers.scope: per gateway running on a virtual machine
qualifiers.condition: gateway runs on a virtual machine

evidence.quote: The maximum supported size of the local cache for a gateway running on a virtual machine is 64 TiB.

claim: Amazon S3 File Gateway supports the S3 Standard, S3 Intelligent-Tiering, S3 Standard-IA and S3 One Zone-IA storage classes.
question: Which Amazon S3 storage classes does S3 File Gateway support?

values.display: S3 Standard, S3 Intelligent-Tiering, S3 Standard - Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) and S3 One Zone-IA

qualifiers.scope: Amazon S3 File Gateway, initial storage class of objects the gateway creates

evidence.quote: Amazon S3 File Gateway supports Amazon S3 Standard, S3 Intelligent-Tiering, S3 Standard - Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) and S3 One Zone-IA.

note: The user guide page storage-classes also lists the Glacier storage class (through lifecycle) and says S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval is not supported.

claim: With S3 File Gateway you set the initial storage class of the objects the gateway creates, and you can then use bucket lifecycle policies to move files from Amazon S3 to Amazon S3 Glacier.
question: How do files in S3 File Gateway reach S3 Glacier?

values.display: bucket lifecycle policies to move files from Amazon S3 to Amazon S3 Glacier

evidence.quote: You configure the initial storage class for objects that the gateway creates, and then you can use bucket lifecycle policies to move files from Amazon S3 to Amazon S3 Glacier.

claim: Amazon S3 File Gateway supports SMB versions 2 and 3 as well as NFS versions 3, 4.0, and 4.1.
question: Which SMB and NFS versions does Amazon S3 File Gateway support?

values.display: SMB versions 2 and 3 as well as NFS versions 3, 4.0, and 4.1

evidence.quote: Amazon S3 File Gateway supports SMB versions 2 and 3 as well as NFS versions 3, 4.0, and 4.1.

claim: Once objects are stored in S3 by S3 File Gateway, you can access them directly in AWS for in-cloud workloads without requiring the gateway.
question: Can I directly access objects stored in S3 by using Amazon S3 File Gateway?

values.display: access them directly in AWS for in-cloud workloads

evidence.quote: Yes. Once objects are stored in S3, you can access them directly in AWS for in-cloud workloads without requiring Amazon S3 File Gateway. Your objects inherit the properties of the S3 bucket in which they are stored, such as lifecycle management, and cross-region replication.

claim: An object that is accessed through a file share should be managed only by the gateway; directly overwriting or updating an object that S3 File Gateway wrote gives undefined behavior when the object is read through the file share.
question: What happens if I overwrite an object in S3 that S3 File Gateway wrote?

values.display: undefined behavior

qualifiers.scope: Amazon S3 File Gateway objects accessed through a file share

evidence.quote: An object that needs to be accessed by using a file share should only be managed by the gateway. If you directly overwrite or update an object previously written by Amazon S3 File Gateway, it results in undefined behavior when the object is accessed through the file share.

claim: If a bucket already contains objects when you configure it for S3 File Gateway, the object keys are used to present the objects as files to NFS and SMB clients, with default file system metadata.
question: What if my bucket already contains objects?

values.display: object keys will be used to present the objects as files

qualifiers.scope: Amazon S3 File Gateway, bucket that already holds objects

evidence.quote: If your bucket already contains objects when you configure it for use with Amazon S3 File Gateway, object keys will be used to present the objects as files to the NFS and SMB clients. The files are given default file system metadata.

claim: S3 File Gateway scans only the object headers for file metadata when you explicitly list files or directories, and it downloads file contents only when the object is read.
question: Does S3 File Gateway download the whole bucket or file contents up front?

values.display: file contents are downloaded only when the object is read

evidence.quote: To reduce latency and number of Amazon S3 requests, Amazon S3 File Gateway only scans the headers for file metadata associated with the objects when you explicitly list the files or directories. File metadata is collected as a part of that scan; file contents are downloaded only when the object is read.

claim: S3 File Gateway does not do data reduction (deduplication or compression); it maps files to objects one-to-one without modification, so you can read the data directly in S3 without the gateway.
question: Does Amazon S3 File Gateway perform data reduction (deduplication or compression)?

values.display: mapped to objects one-to-one

evidence.quote: No. Files are mapped to objects one-to-one in your bucket without modification, enabling you to access your data directly in S3 without needing to use the gateway or deploy additional software to rehydrate your data.

claim: S3 File Gateway does not use the accelerated endpoints, even if the bucket is configured for S3 Transfer Acceleration.
question: Can I use Amazon S3 File Gateway with Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration?

values.display: will not use the accelerated endpoints

qualifiers.condition: bucket configured for S3 Transfer Acceleration

evidence.quote: File Gateway will not use the accelerated endpoints even if your bucket is configured for S3 Transfer Acceleration.

claim: You can create up to 50 file shares for an S3 bucket in a single gateway. The number of file shares per bucket across multiple gateways is not limited, but each gateway is limited to 50 shares.
question: How many file shares can I create per gateway?

values.display: 50 shares

qualifiers.condition: per gateway; no limit per bucket across multiple gateways

evidence.quote: You can create up to 50 shares for an S3 bucket in a single gateway. We do not limit the number of file shares per bucket across multiple gateways but each gateway is limited to 50 shares.

claim: The maximum size of an individual file on S3 File Gateway is 5 TB; if you write a larger file you get a "file too large" error and only the first 5 TB is uploaded.
question: What is the maximum size of an individual file on S3 File Gateway?

values.display: 5 TB

qualifiers.scope: per file on Amazon S3 File Gateway
qualifiers.condition: the FAQ gives the S3 object maximum as the reason

evidence.quote: The maximum size of an individual file is 5 TB, which is the maximum size of an individual object in S3. If you write a file larger than 5 TB, you will get a "file too large" error message and only the first 5 TB of the file will be uploaded.

note: The FAQ ties the file limit to the S3 object maximum. S3 raised the object maximum to 50 TB (chapter 21 fact s3-change-max-object-size-50-tb-2025-12); the user guide quota page fgw-quotas states 5 TiB for the gateway itself. Teach 5 TiB as the gateway limit and do not state 5 TB as the S3 maximum.
